subject: English
summaryPoints: The eight parts of speech (noun, pronoun, verb, adjective, adverb, preposition, conjunction, interjection) define the grammatical function and syntactic distribution of lexical items within an English sentence.

The future perfect tense ('will have + V3') designates an action that will be concluded or achieved prior to a specific baseline deadline or event in future time, frequently accompanied by 'by', 'by the time', or 'before'.

Adverbial clauses of purpose indicate the objective or motive of an action using 'so that' and 'in order that' (which take modal auxiliaries such as 'can', 'could', 'may', 'will', or 'would'), or 'in order to' and 'so as to' (which take bare infinitives).

The conjunction of negative purpose 'lest' conveys 'for fear that' or 'to prevent'; it is followed by the subject and the modal 'should' or a bare present subjunctive verb, and it strictly forbids the insertion of an additional negative particle ('not').

Triphthongs are phonetic units consisting of three consecutive vowel qualities articulated within a single syllable, formed by a diphthong gliding into a terminating schwa /ə/ (e.g., /eɪə/ in layer, /aɪə/ in fire, /ɔɪə/ in royal, /aʊə/ in power, /əʊə/ in lower).

Standard suffixation orthography requires: changing final 'y' to 'i' after a consonant before adding suffixes (e.g., sunny -> sunnier), dropping silent final 'e' before vowel suffixes (care -> caring), and doubling final consonants in stressed monosyllabic or end-accented words (tan -> tanning, prefer -> preferred).

formulas.label: Future Perfect Tense Formula
formulas.expr: Subject + will have + V3(past participle) + by / before + Future Time Expression  OR  by the time + Subject + V1

formulas.label: Adverbial Clause of Purpose with Modal
formulas.expr: Main Clause + so that / in order that + Subject + can / could / may / will / would + V1(base)

formulas.label: Negative Purpose Clause with 'Lest'
formulas.expr: Main Clause + lest + Subject + (should) + V1(bare verb)  [Note: 'not' is prohibited after lest]

formulas.label: Infinitive Purpose Phrase Formula
formulas.expr: Main Clause + in order to / so as to + V1(bare infinitive)

examTip: In EUEE purpose clause items, be extremely vigilant with 'lest': because 'lest' already means 'so that...not' or 'for fear that', it must NEVER contain 'not' (e.g., 'He walked quietly lest he should wake the baby', NOT 'lest he should not wake'). For future perfect questions, look for 'by the time' paired with a simple present verb: 'By the time she graduates, she will have completed the project.'

keyDefinitions.definition: A verbal construction formed with 'will have' plus a past participle that expresses an action projected to be completed before a designated future moment.
A subordinate adverbial clause introduced by 'so that', 'in order that', or 'lest' that clarifies the intended objective or expected aim of the matrix verb.
A formal subordinating conjunction of negative purpose meaning 'for fear that' or 'in order to prevent', taking a subjunctive or 'should' construction without negative words.
A phonetic combination of three vowel sounds pronounced together in a single unbroken syllable, consisting of a diphthong gliding into a schwa /ə/.

eueeFocusTopics: Future perfect tense construction paired with 'by / by the time' temporal markers
Purpose clauses using 'so that' / 'in order that' + modal auxiliaries
Negative purpose clause syntax using 'lest + should + base verb'
Phrasal verbs based on 'look' ('look up to', 'look down on', 'look into', 'look forward to')
